name: planck
why: A standalone ClojureScript REPL with a JavaScriptCore core, but deprecated and mostly a runtime curiosity.

brief.what_it_is: Planck is a stand-alone ClojureScript REPL for macOS and Linux, built on JavaScriptCore. You launch it from the terminal with `planck` or `plk`, then type ClojureScript at the prompt or run script files. It can read files, shell out to other programs, and use a subset of clojure.core, clojure.java.io, and clojure.java.shell under the planck.core, planck.io, and planck.shell namespaces. The README's example reads a file line by line and calls the macOS `say` command.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches it as launching instantly and being useful for scripting, so ClojureScript can serve as a quick scripting language without a heavy JVM toolchain. The README says the ported functions let you write Clojure-idiomatic scripts.
brief.how_it_works: Planck runs ClojureScript on the JavaScriptCore engine, with native-style I/O and shell functions supplied by planck.io and planck.shell. The `plk` script wraps `planck` and calls the `clojure` CLI so that deps.edn and classpath options such as -Aalias work. The build compiles through Closure optimization unless you pass --fast.

brief.install_notes: On macOS, `brew install planck`. On Ubuntu, add the PPA and apt-get install (the README says apt-get install planck after the PPA is added). Other Linux distros need a binary from planck-repl.org/binaries/ or a source build. Building needs OS-specific tooling described on the project's Building wiki page, and build-envs repo offers prebuilt build environments. No accounts or runtime setup are mentioned.
brief.standout: Planck is a ClojureScript REPL with no JVM and a fast start, aimed at shell-style scripting. The plk wrapper bridges it to the Clojure CLI and deps.edn, so Clojure-style dependency management still works.
brief.status: Unknown as to release date. The README and build instructions are current and the copyright line runs to 2024, but I did not see a last-release or last-commit date. The scout notes call the project deprecated, but the README I read says nothing about deprecation, so I could not confirm that.
brief.caveats: macOS and Linux only; the README names no Windows support. Source builds require OS-specific setup from a wiki. The ported functions are a listed subset of Clojure's API, not the full library. The README says nothing about deprecation, which contradicts the scout note.

judge.reason: A standalone ClojureScript runtime atop JavaScriptCore makes shell scripting in ClojureScript possible without a JVM—a genuinely unusual language/runtime pairing.

entry.title: Planck
entry.tldr: A ClojureScript REPL that starts instantly with no JVM, so Clojure-flavoured scripting works from the shell like a quick scripting language.
entry.deeper_look:
Planck is a stand-alone ClojureScript REPL for macOS and Linux, built on JavaScriptCore, the JavaScript engine from WebKit. You run `planck` (or `plk`) in a terminal, then type ClojureScript at the prompt or point it at a script file.

ClojureScript normally means a JVM-based toolchain compiling to JavaScript. Planck skips that at run time. It evaluates ClojureScript on JavaScriptCore directly, and supplies file and process access through ported namespaces: planck.core, planck.io and planck.shell, which cover a subset of clojure.core, clojure.java.io and clojure.java.shell. The README's example reads a file line by line and hands each line to the macOS `say` command.

The idea underneath is that a language usually run as a big compiled project can also be a small scripting tool, if the runtime starts fast. The project's own pitch is: "Planck launches instantly and is useful for scripting." The `plk` wrapper calls the `clojure` CLI so deps.edn and options like -Aalias still work, which keeps Clojure-style dependency handling available.

Homebrew lists the formula as deprecated. The README the brief draws on says nothing about that, so check the repository before relying on it.
entry.install:
brew install planck
# Ubuntu: sudo add-apt-repository ppa:mfikes/planck && sudo apt-get install planck
# Other Linux: prebuilt binaries at https://planck-repl.org/binaries/ or build from source
